label: Benjamin Edmund Murphy, If Nothing Existed Could Anything Be True?
author: Benjamin Edmund Murphy
work: If Nothing Existed Could Anything Be True?, Analítica (Universidad de Panamá) 1 (2021–2022), pp. 52–66
citation_system: printed page numbers of the journal issue
notes: Open-access journal article, publisher-hosted PDF. Secondary witness for David Armstrong's naturalism: the paper defines naturalism as the doctrine that nothing exists apart from spatio-temporal objects (and that all of them are contingent) and reports that Armstrong was a naturalist in this sense, citing Armstrong, Sketch for a Systematic Metaphysics (2010), p. 1. Armstrong's own texts (A World of States of Affairs, 1997; Sketch, 2010) have no pinnable witness: the NDPR review that quotes Sketch p. 1 refuses automated fetches (HTTP 403), and no legitimately hosted copy of either book was found. Only hashes, locators and a short incipit are committed.
